```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(phyloseq)
library(ggplot2)
library(here)
```

```{r}
# --- 1. Chargement des données ---
# On définit le chemin vers le dossier de données à partir de la racine
# here() pointera toujours vers "~/Desktop/VDB/poster_VDB" si ton projet y est créé.
path_data <- "data/raw"
path_figs <- "results/figures"

# Métadonnées
meta_df <- read.csv(here(path_data, "metadata500_starters.csv"), row.names = 1)

# Table d'abondance (ASV table) - 16S
otu_df <- read.csv(here(path_data, "sourdough_tab_16S.csv"), row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)

# Table de taxonomie - 16S
tax_df <- read.csv(here(path_data, "sourdough_tax_16S.csv"), row.names = 1)
```


```{r}
# --- 2. Nettoyage et Préparation ---

# A. Nettoyage et Renommage de la Taxonomie
tax_mat <- tax_df %>%
  # On renomme les colonnes existantes
  rename(
    Kingdom = taxonomy1,
    Phylum  = taxonomy2,
    Class   = taxonomy3,
    Order   = taxonomy4,
    Family  = taxonomy5,
    Genus   = taxonomy6,
    Species = taxonomy7,
    ASV = taxonomy8
  ) %>%
  as.matrix()

# B. Conversion en matrices pour phyloseq
otu_mat <- as.matrix(otu_df)

# C. Vérification de la correspondance des IDs
# Les noms de colonnes de l'OTU table doivent correspondre aux noms de lignes des métadonnées
common_samples <- intersect(colnames(otu_mat), rownames(meta_df))
print(paste("Nombre d'échantillons conservés :", length(common_samples)))

# On filtre pour ne garder que ce qui match
otu_mat <- otu_mat[, common_samples]
meta_df <- meta_df[common_samples, ]

# --- 3. Création de l'objet Phyloseq ---
ps_16s <- phyloseq(
  otu_table(otu_mat, taxa_are_rows = TRUE),
  tax_table(tax_mat),
  sample_data(meta_df)
)

# Petit nettoyage final : enlever les taxons avec 0 abondance (si existants après filtrage sample)
ps_16s <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps_16s) > 0, ps_16s)

print(ps_16s)
```

```{r}
# PCA
dist_mat <- phyloseq::distance(ps_16s, method = "bray")
pcoa_result <- ordinate(ps_16s, method = "PCoA", distance = dist_mat)

eigenvalues <- pcoa_result$values$Relative_eig
cat("Variance expliquée par les 10 premiers axes:\n")
print(cumsum(eigenvalues)[1:10])

n_axes <- which(cumsum(eigenvalues) >= 0.75)[1]  # Premier axe qui atteint 75%
cat("\nNombre d'axes retenus pour capturer 75% de variance:", n_axes, "\n")

# Clustering
coords <- pcoa_result$vectors[, 1:n_axes]

set.seed(42)
kmeans_result <- kmeans(coords, centers = 4, nstart = 25, iter.max = 100)
clusters <- kmeans_result$cluster

sample_data(ps_16s)$Cluster <- as.factor(clusters)
```



```{r}
p_kmeans <- plot_ordination(ps_16s, ord_pcoa, color = "Cluster")
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
```

```{r}

#ten_samples <- sample_names(ps_rel)[1:10]

random_ten_samples <- sample(sample_names(ps_16s), 10)

ps_subset <- prune_samples(random_ten_samples, ps_16s)

# 1. On agglomère au niveau du Genre (pour simplifier)
ps_genus <- tax_glom(ps_subset, taxrank = "Genus")

# 2. On transforme en abondance relative (pourcentage)
ps_rel <- transform_sample_counts(ps_genus, function(x) x / sum(x))

# 3. On garde seulement les Top 10 Genres les plus abondants au total
top10 <- names(sort(taxa_sums(ps_rel), decreasing = TRUE))[1:10]
ps_top10 <- prune_taxa(top10, ps_rel)

# 4. Conversion en dataframe pour ggplot
df_top10 <- psmelt(ps_top10)

# 5. Graphique
p1 <- ggplot(df_top10, aes(x = Sample, y = Abundance, fill = Genus)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Composition bactérienne (Top 10 Genres)", y = "Abondance Relative") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), # On cache les noms des samples car illisibles (500 samples)
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank())

print(p1)
```

Faires des cluster (unsupervised faire avec differents k)
représenter 5 ou 10 random sample par cluster 

```{r}
pcoa_coords <- ord_pcoa$vectors[, 1:2]

library(ggplot2)

# Tester de 2 à 10 clusters
wss <- sapply(2:10, function(k) {
  kmeans(pcoa_coords, centers = k, nstart = 25)$tot.withinss
})

# Créer un petit dataframe pour le graphique "Elbow"
elbow_df <- data.frame(k = 2:10, wss = wss)

# Graphique de l'éboulis
ggplot(elbow_df, aes(x = k, y = wss)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Elbow plot)",
       x = "Nombre de clusters (k)",
       y = "Somme des carrés (WSS)")
```

```{r}
# 2. Plot
```

```{r}
  theme_classic() +

       x = "PCoA 1", # Tu peux personnaliser les noms d'axes ici
       y = "PCoA 2")

print(p3)

ggsave(here(path_figs,"p3.svg"), width=8, height=6)
```


# --- Test différentes distances pour PCA ---

```{r}
ord_pcoa_bray <- ordinate(ps_16s, method = "PCoA", distance = "bray")

plot_data <- plot_ordination(ps_16s, ord_pcoa_bray, color = "Country", justDF = TRUE)

# Extraire les valeurs propres (eigenvalues)
evals <- ord_pcoa_bray$values$Relative_eig

# Calculer le pourcentage pour les deux premiers axes
pc1 <- round(100 * evals[1], 1)
pc2 <- round(100 * evals[2], 1)

p4 <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Axis.1, y = Axis.2, color = Country)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) + # J'ai ajouté alpha (transparence) pour mieux voir les densités
  scale_color_manual(values = c("France" = "#377eb8", "United States" = "#e41a1c")) + 
  theme_classic() +
  labs(title = "Comparaison structurelle : France vs USA",
       x = paste0("PCoA 1 [", pc1, "%]"), # Affiche par ex: PCoA 1 [12.5%]
    y = paste0("PCoA 2 [", pc2, "%]"))

print(p4)
```
```{r}
# 1. Extraire la table d'abondance (ASV en lignes, Samples en colonnes)
otu_tab <- as(otu_table(ps_16s), "matrix")

# 2. Ajouter 1 pour éviter les zéros (pseudocount)
otu_tab_plus1 <- otu_tab + 1

# 3. Calculer la CLR manuellement
# Pour chaque échantillon (colonne), on fait log(x / moyenne_géométrique(x))
clr_tab <- apply(otu_tab_plus1, 2, function(x) {
  log(x) - mean(log(x))
})

# 4. Réinjecter dans un nouvel objet phyloseq
ps_clr_manual <- ps_16s
otu_table(ps_clr_manual) <- otu_table(clr_tab, taxa_are_rows = TRUE)

# 5. Faire l'ordination (Distance Euclidienne sur données CLR = Aitchison)
ord_pcoa_aitchison <- ordinate(ps_clr_manual, method = "PCoA", distance = "euclidean")

plot_data <- plot_ordination(ps_16s, ord_pcoa_aitchison, color = "Country", justDF = TRUE)

# Extraire les valeurs propres (eigenvalues)
evals <- ord_pcoa_aitchison$values$Relative_eig

# Calculer le pourcentage pour les deux premiers axes
pc1 <- round(100 * evals[1], 1)
pc2 <- round(100 * evals[2], 1)

p6 <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Axis.1, y = Axis.2, color = Country)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) + # J'ai ajouté alpha (transparence) pour mieux voir les densités
  scale_color_manual(values = c("France" = "#377eb8", "United States" = "#e41a1c")) + 
  theme_classic() +
  labs(title = "Comparaison structurelle : France vs USA",
       x = paste0("PCoA 1 [", pc1, "%]"), # Affiche par ex: PCoA 1 [12.5%]
    y = paste0("PCoA 2 [", pc2, "%]"))

print(p6)
```


```{r}
library(phyloseq)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggdendro)
library(patchwork)

# --- ÉTAPE 1 : Définir les clusters ---
dist_mat <- phyloseq::distance(ps_16s, method = "bray")
hc <- hclust(dist_mat, method = "average") # method = ward.D2 ou average
clusters <- cutree(hc, k = 4)

# --- ÉTAPE 2 : Fusion MANUELLE par cluster (sans merge_samples) ---
# Extraire la table OTU
otu_mat <- as.matrix(otu_table(ps_16s))

# Si les samples sont en colonnes, transposer si nécessaire
if (!taxa_are_rows(ps_16s)) {
  otu_mat <- t(otu_mat)
}

# Créer une matrice fusionnée (somme par cluster)
cluster_names <- paste0("Cluster_", 1:4)
otu_merged <- matrix(0, nrow = nrow(otu_mat), ncol = 4)
rownames(otu_merged) <- rownames(otu_mat)
colnames(otu_merged) <- cluster_names

for (i in 1:4) {
  samples_in_cluster <- which(clusters == i)
  otu_merged[, i] <- rowSums(otu_mat[, samples_in_cluster, drop = FALSE])
}

# Créer le nouvel objet phyloseq
ps_merged <- phyloseq(
  otu_table(otu_merged, taxa_are_rows = TRUE),
  tax_table(ps_16s),
  sample_data(data.frame(
    Cluster = factor(cluster_names),
    row.names = cluster_names
  ))
)

# Transformation en abondance relative
ps_merged_rel <- transform_sample_counts(ps_merged, function(x) x / sum(x))

# --- ÉTAPE 3 : Dendrogramme ---
dist_merged <- phyloseq::distance(ps_merged_rel, method = "bray")
hc_merged <- hclust(dist_merged, method = "average") # method = ward.D2 ou average
dendro_data <- dendro_data(as.dendrogram(hc_merged))

p_tree <- ggplot(segment(dendro_data)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend)) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(b = 0, unit = "cm"))

# --- ÉTAPE 4 : Barplot ---
ps_genus <- tax_glom(ps_merged_rel, taxrank = "Genus", NArm = TRUE)
top10 <- names(sort(taxa_sums(ps_genus), decreasing = TRUE))[1:10]
ps_top10 <- prune_taxa(top10, ps_genus)
df_top10 <- psmelt(ps_top10)

order_leaves <- dendro_data$labels$label[order(dendro_data$labels$x)]
df_top10$Sample <- factor(df_top10$Sample, levels = order_leaves)
df_top10$Genus <- as.character(df_top10$Genus)
df_top10$Genus[is.na(df_top10$Genus)] <- "Non classifié"

p_bar <- ggplot(df_top10, aes(x = Sample, y = Abundance, fill = Genus)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Paired") +
  labs(y = "Abondance Relative", x = "Cluster") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 0, unit = "cm")
  )

# --- ÉTAPE 5 : Assemblage ---
final_plot <- p_tree / p_bar + plot_layout(heights = c(1, 3))
print(final_plot)
```
